Title: Constructing a Molotov Cocktail at range

Messages.Author: Fred Scott
Messages.Body:
Molotov Cocktail
Combat
Strike: put this card on this minion, it becomes an equipment card: a weapon.
Beginning with the next round of this combat, the bearer can strike with this
weapon for 2R aggravated damage. Burn this card after use or when combat
ends.

I can't think of any reason in the rules why it would be legal to arm
yourself with a Molotov Cocktail at long range, bizarre as it seems.
Apparently, you have to be at close range - although you can ultimately
strike _with_ the MC at long range after you've armed yourself with it.

Can anyone confirm or deny this? Gad, that's silly! It's as if you need
your enemy close by to maybe hold the flashlight or something so you can
see to stuff the rag in the bottle of gasoline. WtF?

I know cards can be like this, of course. This one just struck me as being
a bit over the top.... (grouse, grumble, whine!)

Fred

Yes, I can deny it.

Strikes that fail to specify R or Ranged can be played at any range.
They will simply fail to have any effect on your opponent.
As the strike to acquire the Cocktail does not have any effect on your
opponent, range is immaterial.

Compare to Dodge.
Clearly, dodge can be played at every range.

Excellent. I hope my conclusion was wrong, but...

> Strikes that fail to specify R or Ranged can be played at any range.
> They will simply fail to have any effect on your opponent.

The wording used in rule 6.4.3 (under the bullet list bullet that begins,
"Resolve Strike."): "...Most strikes are effective only at close range.
Unless the strike is identified as ranged or does 'R' damage (or is a
defensive strike such as dodge or combat ends), it is only effective at
close range. Ranged strikes and strikes that do 'R' damage can be used
at any range, close or long."

I guess I assumed the word "effective", in the context of a strike that
equips a minion would mean that the minion was allowed to equip. If the
strike were not "effective", it wouldn't be allowed to equip. I guess
I didn't really think in terms of equipping being considered a defensive
strike because it isn't preventing any offensive strike effects from
taking place as dodges and combat ends do. But I suppose that's not
strictly defined and obviously, it makes sense. If equipping with the
Cocktail qualifies as such, if that's precisely what is meant by this
rule, I would think maybe the term "non-offensive strike" would convey
the meaning better than "defensive strike".

> As the strike to acquire the Cocktail does not have any effect on your
> opponent, range is immaterial.

Well, OK. I just can't find where that criteria is spelled out in the
rules as you're quoting it.

OK, cool. I thought of a follow-up question. I assume, then, that a Strike:
Dodge (and, when something like a Telepathic Tracking is played, Strike:
Combat Ends) does the same thing as being at long range in the sense that
it evades your opponents offensive strike effects (damage, steal blood,
effects like Coma, and so forth) but does not prevent other kinds of

I guess this is why a Dodge doesn't cancel a Strike: Combat Ends.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <Qt6Gf.28967$JT.12803@fed1read06>, Fred Scott

<nos...@no.spam.dot.com> writes:
>I assume, then, that a Strike:
>Dodge (and, when something like a Telepathic Tracking is played, Strike:
>Combat Ends) does the same thing as being at long range in the sense that
>it evades your opponents offensive strike effects (damage, steal blood,
>effects like Coma, and so forth) but does not prevent other kinds of
>effects (for instance, equipping with a Molotov Cocktail) from occurring.

The effects of a Dodge are explicitly defined in the rulebook:

"A dodge strike deals no damage, but it protects the dodging
minion and his possessions from the effects of the opposing
strike."

Since a "Put a card on this striking minion" effect is in no way an
effect against the opposing minion or his possessions, a Dodge in no way
alters that effect.

If the stike is lost, then the opposing minion would fail to equip with
the Molotov Cocktail. So the upshot is, if Methuselah A's minion arms
with a Molotov Cocktail in the first round of a combat while his opponent
in the combat, Methuselah B, plays Strike: Combat ends for his minion
and then Methuselah A plays Telepathic Tracking at superior, then the
combat continues but Methuselah A's minion failed to equip and the MC
is not placed on it. Methuselah A's minion must start over with another
Molotov Cocktail card in the second round. Is that correct?

Fred
